type_name: Certified efficient IT and end-user equipment
definition: IT and end-user equipment (computers, servers, devices, network equipment) required to meet a recognised energy-efficiency standard or certification such as Energy Star. Does not include network design or technology changes, cooling, or buildings.

Network design or technology choices made to reduce energy use (more efficient radio technologies, fibre instead of copper, power-saving network modes). Does not include certification of equipment, cooling or buildings.

Buildings and facilities, including data centres, designed or certified for energy efficiency (EDGE, LEED or similar, power usage effectiveness targets). Does not include cooling systems alone or the equipment inside.
Cooling systems chosen to reduce electricity use. Does not include whole-building certification.
Systems that monitor or control energy use to reduce it (smart meters for the project's own sites, energy management systems). Does not include efficiency of the equipment itself.
Replacing existing inefficient technology (2G sites, copper lines, old equipment) specifically to save energy. Does not include buying new efficient equipment where nothing is replaced.
Uses equipment selected for lower energy consumption
Applies a defined efficiency benchmark to project-financed equipment
